content.comment_body: Hello, If I have four [product_name] modules set up in a master/master communication configuration, is it possible to place an [product_name] operator device on the network and control all four modules through it? Or is it limited to controlling only one module as a server? Thank you, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Based on your description, this setup should work. You can refer to the TIA Portal Help by searching for "[product_name] operator device" and checking the communication details. According to the information, a single panel can handle up to four [product_name] modules with [article_no]. There are examples available for programming this configuration. You can: - Adapt the example to a physical panel using four connections - Simulate a panel with four connections - Simulate four panels each with one connection Let me know if any of these options solve your requirements. Regards

analysis.insight_summary: The user is looking to determine whether a single [product_name] operator device can manage multiple [product_name] modules connected in a master/master network. The conversation highlights that, with proper configuration via TIA Portal and panel settings, an operator device can connect to and control up to four modules. Programming examples are available to assist, and users are encouraged to try both real and simulated setups.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that one [product_name] operator device can manage all four [product_name] modules in the network rather than being restricted to only one.
